output.brief:
The buffering in Kestria is not coming from the new CDN. It comes from smart-TV app version 5.2. That release cut the player's startup buffer from 10 s to 4 s. Kestria was the only market where it was rolled out, and it went live on 9 October, the same time as the CDN cutover. Session data shows 5.2 TVs stalling about 5.9% of viewing time on every ISP. Every other client on the same CDN and ISPs stalls about 0.6–0.7%. Employee test TVs on the old CDN, Corvane, already showed 5.7% stalling before launch. The handball launch and ISP congestion don't fit the data. I'm about 90% sure.

Next steps:
1. Revert Kestria to the 5.1 streaming settings and hold the 20 November wider rollout. This is a server-side config change that takes about an hour.
2. Don't send the SLA breach notice, withhold fees or move traffic back to Corvane.
3. Keep the Kestria alert on. Muting it would hide the problem.
4. Add app version and device breakdowns to the dashboard. The pipeline work for that is about six weeks out.
5. Hold off on the cancellation offer. The 1 October price rise also affects cancellations, so buffering's share of them is not established.
